pointers.sentence: A new project has no user, and the admin, where users are added, admits only an active staff user ([The site's own pages: the index, the login and `AdminSite.each_context`](../admin/site-views.md)) (`django/contrib/admin/sites.py:AdminSite.has_permission`). createsuperuser makes the first from the command line, for whatever model `AUTH_USER_MODEL` names, so it knows of the fields only what the model declares: the field named by `USERNAME_FIELD`, those of `AbstractBaseUser.REQUIRED_FIELDS`, and whether there is a field called `"password"`.

If the model has a field called `"password"`, the data starts with a password of `None`, meaning none given yet; a model without one is never asked for a password (`django/contrib/auth/management/commands/createsuperuser.py:Command.handle`).

When the stream is not a TTY it raises `NotRunningInTTYException`, which `handle` catches at its end: it writes that creation was skipped and ends without an error, so a script that forgets `--noinput` and runs without a terminal makes no user and does not fail (`django/contrib/auth/management/commands/createsuperuser.py:Command.handle`).
When `AUTH_USER_MODEL` names another model there is none, since, a comment says, no assumption can be made about the username then (`django/contrib/auth/management/__init__.py:get_default_username`).

`Command.get_input_data` reads an answer with `input`, puts the default in place of an empty one, and has the model field clean it; an error is written and the question asked again (`django/contrib/auth/management/commands/createsuperuser.py:Command.get_input_data`).
A foreign key is answered with the key of a row that must exist (`django/db/models/fields/related.py:ForeignKey.validate`).
A field that may be blank may be given empty, and is then left out (`django/contrib/auth/management/commands/createsuperuser.py:Command.handle`).

`UserManager.create_superuser` sets `is_staff=True` and `is_superuser=True`, raises `ValueError` if told otherwise, and makes the user as `UserManager.create_user` does (`django/contrib/auth/models.py:UserManager.create_superuser`).

`UserManager.create_superuser` validates no password; the documentation gives two reasons: developers, not users, work at that level, and a model's validation does not run as it is created (`docs/topics/auth/passwords.txt`).

changepassword looks the user up by `USERNAME_FIELD`, under the name given or else the system account's from `getpass.getuser`, taken as it is; a name no user has is a `CommandError` (`django/contrib/auth/management/commands/changepassword.py:Command.handle`).
